A familiar cannot attack, but it is able take other actions as normal. If it drops to 0 hitpoints, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form. It reappears after you cast this spell again. As an action, you may temporarily dismiss your familiar to a pocket dimension, or dismiss it forever. As an action while it is temporarily dismissed, you may cause it to reappear in any unoccupied space within 30ft. of you. Whenever the familiar drops to 0 hitpoints or disappears into the pocket dimension, it leaves behind in its space anything it was wearing or carrying.

While your familiar is within 100ft. of you, you may communicate with it telepathically. Additionally, as an action, you are able to see through your familiar's eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining the benefits of any special senses that the familiar has. During this time, you are deafened and blinded with regard to your own senses.

You cannot have more than one familiar at a time. If you cast this spell while you already have a familiar, you instead cause it to adopt a new form. Choose one of the forms from the above list for your familiar to transform into.

Finally, when you cast a spell with a range of touch, your familiar may instead deliver the spell as if it had cast the spell. Your familiar must be within 100ft. of you, and it must use its reaction to deliver the spell when you cast it. If the spell requires an attack roll, you use your attack modifier for the roll.

Grasping weeds and vines sprout from the ground in a 20ft. square starting from a point within range. For the duration, these plants turn the ground in the area into difficult terrain. Any creature in the area when you cast the spell must succeed on a STR saving throw, or be restrained by the entangling plants until the spell ends. A creature restrained by the plants may use its action to make a STR check. On a success, it frees itself.
When the spell ends, the conjured plants wilt away.

The next time you hit a creature with a weapon attack before this spell ends, a writhing mass of thorny vines appears at the point of impact, and the target must succeed on a STR saving throw, or be restrained by the magical vines for the duration. A Large or larger creature gains advantage on this saving throw. If the target succeeds on the save, the vines shrivel away.

While restrained by this spell, the target takes {*}d6 @piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature restrained by the vines, or one that can touch the creature, may use its action to make a STR check. On a success, the target is freed.

feather-fall.name: Feather Fall

castTime.condition: you or a creature within 60ft. of you falls

vsm: a small feather or piece of down

desc.desc: Choose up to 5 falling creatures within range. A falling creature's rate of descent slows to 60ft. per round until the spell ends. If the creature lands before the spell ends, it takes no falling damage, and may land on its feet, ending the spell for that creature.

longstrider.name: Longstrider
vsm: a pinch of dirt

desc.desc: You touch {*} creature(s). For the duration, a target's speed increases by 10ft.

Blazing orbs of fire plummet to the ground at 4 different points you can see within range. Each creature in a 40ft. radius sphere centered on each point must make a DEX saving throw, taking 20d6 @fire damage + 20d6 @bludgeoning damage on a failed save, of half as much on a successful one. The sphere spreads around corners. A creature in the area of more than one meteor is affected only once.

jump.name: Jump
vsm: a grasshopper's hind leg

desc.desc: You touch a creature. The creature's jump distance is tripled until the spell ends.

As you hold out your hands with thumbs touching and fingers spread, a thin sheet of flames shoots forth from your outstretched fingertips. Each creature in a 15ft. cone must make a DEX saving throw, taking {*}d6 @fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. The fire ignites any flammable objects in the area that are not being worn or carried.

demacian-justice.name: Demacian Justice
vsm: a silvered greatsword

desc.quote: "Justice; by law, or by sword" - Garen

desc.desc: You call on the might of Demacia, and it will respond to your call in all its glory and power. Choose a creature within range. The creature will be smitten by a sword of holy light descending from the skies, dealing 15d10 @radiant damage.

This damage is completely unavoidable; it is unaffected by resistances and immunities, cannot be dispelled by a 9th-level @counterspell spell, and ignores any traits and abilities that would otherwise lower or prevent this damage.

astral-projection.name: Astral Projection
vsm: a jacinth worth at least 1000gp, and an ornately carved bar of silver worth at least 100gp, both once for each creature you affect with this spell, all of which the spell consumes

desc.desc: You and up to 8 willing creatures within range project your astral bodies into the Astral Plane. The spell fails if you are aleady on that plane. The material body you leave behind is unconscious, and in a state of suspended animation; it doesn't need food or air, and doesn't age.

Your astral body resembles your mortal form in almost every way, replicating your game statistics and possessions. The principal difference is the addition of a silvery cord that extends from between your shoulder blades and trails behind you, fading to invisibility after 1ft. This cord is your tether to your material body. As long as the tether remains intact, you can find your way home. If the cord is cut - something that may happen only when an effect specifically states that it does - your soul and body are separated, killing you instantly.

Your astral form may freely travel through the Astral Plane, and may pass through portals there leading to any other plane. If you enter a new plane or return to the plane you were on when casting this spell, your body and possessions are transported along the silver cord, allowing you to re-enter your body as you enter the new plane. Your astral form is a separate incarnation. The spell ends for you and your companions when you use your action to dismiss it. When the spell ends, the affected creature returns to its physical body, and it awakens.

The spell might also end early for you or one of your companions; a successful @dispel magic spell used against an astral or physical body ends the spell for that creature. If a creature's original body or its astral form drops to 0 hitpoints, the spell ends for that creature. If the spell ends and the silver cord is intact, the cord pulls the creature's astral form back into its body, ending its state of suspended animation. If you are returned to your body prematurely, your companions remain in their astral forms and must find their own way back to their bodies, usually by dropping to 0 hitpoints.

You create a blade-shaped, planar rift about 3ft. long in an unoccupied space you can see within range. Whenever you cast this spell, and as a bonus action on each of your subsequent turns, you may make up to 2 melee spell attacks with the blade, each one against a creature, loose object, or structure within 5ft. of the blade. On a hit, the target takes 4d12 @force damage. This attack scores a critical hit if the number on the d20 is 18 or higher. On a critical hit, the blade deals an extra 8d12, for a total of 12d12 @force damage.
The blade is able to harmlessly pass through any barrier, including a @wall of force spell.

foresight.name: Foresight
vsm: a hummingbird feather

desc.desc: You touch a willing creature, and bestow a limited ability to see into the immediate future. For the duration, the target cannot be surprised, and gains advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws. Other creatures gain disadvantage on attack rolls against the target. The spell ends early if you cast it again before the duration ends.
The blade is able to harmlessly pass through any barrier, including a @wall of force spell.

gate.name: Gate
vsm: a diamond worth at least 500gp

desc.desc: You conjure a portal, linking an unoccupied space you can see within range to a precise location on a different plane of existence. The portal is a circular opening, which you may make 5 to 20ft. in diameter. You may orient the portal in any direction you choose.

The portal has a front and a back on each plane where it appears. Travel through the portal is possible only by moving through its front. Anything that does so is instantly transported to the other plane, appearing in the unoccupied space nearest to the portal.
Deities, and other planar rulers, may prevent portals created by this spell from opening in their presence, or anywhere within their domains.

Whenever you cast this spell, you may speak the name of a specific creature (a pseudonym, title, or nickname does not work). If that creature is on a plane other than the one you are on, the portal opens in the named creature's immediate vicinity, and draws the creature through it to the nearest unoccupied space on your side of the portal. You gain no special power over the creature, and it is free to act as the DM deems appropriate. It might leave, attack you, or help you.

imprisonment.name: Imprisonment
vsm: a vellum depiction, or a carved statuette in the likeness of the target, and a special component that varies according to the version of the spell you choose, worth at least 500gp per hit die of the target

desc.desc: You create a magical restraint to hold a creature that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a WIS saving throw, or be bound by the spell. On a success, it is immune to the spell if you cast it again. While affected by this spell, the creature does not need to eat, drink, or breathe, and it doesn't age.

During the casting of the spell, in any of its versions, you may specify a condition that will cause the spell to end and release the target. The condition may be as specific, or as elaborate as you choose, but the DM must agree that the condition is reasonable, and has a likelihood of coming to pass. The conditions may be based on a creature's name, identity, or deity, but otherwise must be based on observable actions or qualities, and not based on intangibles such as level, class, or hitpoints.
A 9th level @dispel magic spell may end the spell early if targeting either the prison, or the special component used to create it.
Whenever you cast the spell, choose one of the following forms of imprisonment:

content: The target is entombed far beneath the earth, in a sphere of magical force that is just large enough to contain the target. Nothing may pass through the sphere, nor may any creature teleport or use planar travel to get into, or out of it.
Heavy chains, firmly rooted in the ground, hold the target in place. The target is restrained until the spell ends, and it cannot move, or be moved by any means, until then.
A fine chain of precious metal.

The spell transports the target into a tiny demiplane that is warded against teleportation and planar travel. The demiplane may be a labyrinth, cage, tower, or any similar confined structure or area of your choice.
A miniature representation of the prison, made from jade.

The target shrinks to a height of 1in., and is imprisoned inside a gemstone or similar object. Light may pass through the gemstone normally, allowing the target to see out, and other creatures to see in, but nothing else may pass through, even by means of teleportation or planar travel. The gemstone cannot be cut or broken while the spell remains in effect.
A large, transparent gemstone, such as a conrundum, diamond, or ruby.
The target falls asleep, and cannot be awoken.

desc.desc: Choose a creature, object, or magical effect within range. Any spell of {*} level or lower on the target ends. For a spell of higher level than this, you must first succeed on an ability check using your spellcasting ability, with DC of 10 + the spell's level.

castTime.condition: you see a creature within 60ft. of you cast a spell

desc.desc: You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell. If the creature is casting a spell of {*} level or lower, its spell fails. For a spell of higher level than this, you must first succeed on an ability check using your spellcasting ability, with DC of 10 + the spell's level.

invulnerability.name: Invulnerability
vsm: a small piece of adamantine worth at least 500gp, which the spell consumes

desc.desc: For the duration, you are immune to all damage.

A flood of healing energy flows from you, into injured creatures around you. You restore up to 700 hitpoints, divided as you choose among any number of creature of your choice that you can see within range that aren't constructs or undead. Creatures healed by this spell are also cured of all diseases, and any effect causing them to be blinded or deafened.

A wave of healing energy washes over a creature you touch. The target regains all its hitpoints. If the creature is charmed, frightened, paralyzed, or stunned, the condition ends. If the creature is prone, it may use its reaction to stand up. This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.
You utter a word of power that is able to compel one creature you can see within range to die instantly. If the creature you chose has 100 hitpoints or fewer, it dies.

You unleash the power of your mind, to blast the intellect of up to 10 creatures of your choice that you can see within range. Creatures that have an INT score of 2 or lower are unaffected. A target must make an INT saving throw, taking 14d6 @psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Additionally, on a failed save, the target is stunned. A stunned target may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turn, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Whenever a creature is killed by this spell, its head explodes, assuming it has one.

time-ravage.name: Time Ravage
vsm: an hourglass filled with diamond dust worth at least 5.000gp, which the spell consumes

desc.desc: You target a creature you can see within range, putting its physical form through the devastation of rapid aging. The target must make a CON saving throw, taking 10d12 @necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Additionally, on a failure, the target also ages to the point where it has only 30 days left before it dies of old age. In this aged satet, the target gains disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws, and its walking speed is halved.
Only the @wish spell, or a 9th level @greater restoration spell may end these effects, and restore the target to its previous age.
You briefly stop the flow of time for everyone but yourself. No time passes for other creatures, while you take 1d4 + 1 turns in a row, during which you may use actions, and move as normal.

The spell ends early if one of the actions you use, or any effects that you create during this period affects a creature other than you, or an object being worn or carried by someone other than you. Additionally, the spell ends early if you move to a place more than 1.000ft. from the location where you cast it.
Wish is the mightiest spell a mortal creature is able to cast. By simply speaking aloud, you may alter the very foundations of reality in accord with your desires.
The basic use of this spell is to duplicate any other spell of 8th level or lower. You don't need to meet any requirements for that spell, including costly components. The spell simply takes effect.
Alternatively, you may create one of the following effects of your choice:

content.desc: You create an object of up to 25.000gp in value that is not a magic item. The object may be no more than 300ft. in any dimension, and it appears in a unoccupied space you can see on the ground.
You allow up to 20 creatures that you can see to regain all hitpoints, and you end all effects on them described in the @greater restoration spell.
You grant up to 10 creatures that you can see resistance to a damage type of your choice.

You grant up to 10 creatures you can see immunity to a single spell, or other magical effect, for 8 hours. For instance, you could make yourself and all your companions immune to a lich's life drain attack.

You undo a single recent event by forcing a reroll of any roll made within the last round, including your last turn. Reality reshapes itself to accommodate the new result. For example, a wish spell could undo an opponent's successful save, a foe's critical hit, or a friend's failed save. You may force the reroll to be made with advantage or disadvantage, and you may choose to use the reroll, or the original roll.

desc.desc: You might be able to achieve something beyond the scope of the above examples. State your wish to the DM as precisely as possible. The DM has great latitude in ruling what occurs in such an instance; the greater the wish, the greater the likelihood that something goes wrong. The spell might simply fail, the effect you desire might only be partially achieved, or you might suffer some unforseen consequence as a result of how you worded the wish. For example, wishing that a villain were dead might propel you forward in time, to a period when that villain is no longer alive, effectively removing you from the game. Similarly, wishing for a legendary magic item or artifact might instantly teleport you to the presence of the item's current owner.

The stress of casting this spell to produce any effect other than duplicating another spell weakens you. After enduring that stress, each time you cast a spell until you finish a long rest, you take 1d10 @necrotic damage per level of that spell. This damage cannot be reduced or prevented in any way. Additionally, your STR score drops to 3 for 2d4 days. For each of those days that you spend resting and doing nothing more than light activity, your remaining recovery time decreases by 2 days. Finally, roll 1d6. On a 1 or a 2, you are unable to cast this spell every again after suffering this stress.

invisibility.name: Invisibility
vsm: an eyelash, encased in gum arabic

desc.desc: {*} creature(s) you touch becomes invisible for the duration. Anything a target is wearing or carrying is invisible, as long as it is on their person. The spell ends early for a target that attacks or casts a spell.

creation.name: Creation
vsm: a tiny piece of matter of the same type of the item you plan to create

desc.desc: You pull wisps of shadow material from the Shadowfell to create a nonliving object of a specific material. The object created may be no larger than a {*}ft. cube, and the object must be of a form and material you have seen before.
The duration depends on the object's material. If the object is composed of multiple materials, use the shortest duration.

You awaken the sense of mortality in {*} creature(s) you can see within range that isn't a construct or undead. Should there be multiple targets, they need to be within 30ft. of each other. A target must succeed on a WIS saving throw, or become frightened of you. The frightened target may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

polymorph.name: Polymorph
vsm: a caterpillar cocoon

desc.desc: You transform a creature of your choice that you can see within range into a new form. An unwilling target must succeed on a WIS saving throw, or be forced to transform. An unwilling shapechanger automatically succeeds on its saving throw.

The transformation lasts for the duration, until the target drops to 0 hitpoints, or dies. The new form may be any beast whose challenge rating is equal to or less than the target's, or half the target's level, if the target does not have a challenge rating. The target's game statistics, including mental ability scores, are replaced by the statistics of the chosen beast. The target retains its hitpoints, alignment, and personality.

The target assumes the hitpoints of its new form. Whenever it reverts to its normal form, the creature returns to the hitpoints it had before it transformed. If it revers as a result of dropping to 0 hitpoints, any excess damage carries over to its normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce the creature's normal form to 0 hitpoints, it isn't knocked unconscious.
The target is limited in the actions it is able to perform by the nature of its new form, and it cannot speak, cast spells, or take any other action that requires hand or speech.
The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature cannot activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its equipment. This spell cannot affect a target that has 0 hitpoints.

mass-polymorph.name: Mass Polymorph
vsm: a caterpillar cocoon

desc.desc: You transform up to 10 creatures of your choice that you can see within range into a new form. An unwilling target must succeed on a WIS saving throw, or be forced to transform. An unwilling shapechanger automatically succeeds on its saving throw.

The transformation lasts for the duration, until the target drops to 0 hitpoints, or dies. The new form may be any beast whose challenge rating is equal to or less than the target's, or half the target's level, if the target does not have a challenge rating. You may choose the same form, or different ones, for each target. The target's game statistics, including mental ability scores, are replaced by the statistics of the chosen beast. The target retains its hitpoints, alignment, and personality.

The target assumes the hitpoints of its new form. Whenever it reverts to its normal form, the creature returns to the hitpoints it had before it transformed. If it revers as a result of dropping to 0 hitpoints, any excess damage carries over to its normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce the creature's normal form to 0 hitpoints, it isn't knocked unconscious.
The target is limited in the actions it is able to perform by the nature of its new form, and it cannot speak, cast spells, or take any other action that requires hand or speech.
The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature cannot activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its equipment. This spell cannot affect a target that has 0 hitpoints.

A shimmering, multicolored plane of light forms a vertical, opaque wall - up to 90ft. long, 30ft., high, and 1in. thick - centered on a point you can see within range. Alternatively, you may shape the wall into a 15ft. radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range. If you position the wall so that it passes through a space occupied by a creature, the spell fails.

The wall sheds bright light out to a range of 100ft., and dim light for an additional 100ft. You and any number of creatures of your choice when you cast the spell may pass through, and remain near the wall without harm. Any other creature that can see the wall and moves to within 20ft. of it, or starts its turn there, must succeed on a CON saving throw, or become blinded for 1 minute.

The wall consists of 7 layers, each with a different color. When a creature attempts to reach into, or pass through the wall, it does so 1 layer at a time, through all the wall's layers. As it passes or reaches through each layer, the creature must make DEX saving throw, and be affected by that layer's properties as described in the table below.

The wall may be destroyed, also 1 layer at a time, in order from red to violet, by means specific to each layer. Once a layer is destroyed, it remains so for the duration of the spell. An @antimagic field spell has no effect on it.

content: The creature takes 10d6 @fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
This layer is destroyed by dealing at least 25 @cold damage to it.
While this layer is in place, nonmagical ranged attacks cannot pass through the wall.
The creature takes 10d6 @acid damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
This layer is destroyed by a strong wind.
While this layer is in place, magical ranged attacks cannot pass through the wall.
The creature takes 10d6 @lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
This layer is destroyed by dealing at least 60 @force damage to it.
The creature takes 10d6 @poison damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
This layer is destroyed by a @passwall spell, or another spell of equal or greater level that is able to open a portal on a solid surface.
The creature takes 10d6 @cold damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
This layer is destroyed by dealing at least 25 @fire damage to it.

On a failure, the creature is restrained. It must then make a CON saving throw at the end of each of its turn. On 3 failures, it permanently turns to stone, and is petrified. On 3 successes, the spell ends. The successes and failures do not need to be consecutive; keep track of both, until the creature collects 3 of a kind.
This layer is destroyed by bright light shed by a @daylight spell, or similar spell of equal or higher level.
While this layer is in place, spells cannot be cast through the wall.

On a failure, the creature is blinded until the start of your next turn. It must then succeed on a WIS saving throw at the start of your next turn, or be transported to another plane of the DM's choosing. Typically, a creature that is on a plane that isn't its home plane is banished home, while other creatures are typically cast into the Astral or Ethereal planes.
This layer is destroyed by a @dispel magic spell, or similar spell of equal or higher level that is able to end spells and magical effects.

ravenous-void.name: Ravenous Void
vsm: a small, nine-pointed star, made of iron

desc.desc: You create a 20ft. radius sphere of destructive gravitation force centered on a point you can see within range. For the duration, the sphere, and any space within 100ft. of it, are difficult terrain, and nonmagical objects fully inside the sphere are destroyed if they aren't being worn or carried.

Whenever the sphere appears, and at the start of each of your turns until the spell ends, unsecured objects within 100ft. of the sphere are pulled toward the sphere's center, ending in an unoccupied space as close to the center as possible.

A creature that starts its turn within 100ft. of the sphere must succeed on a STR saving throw, or be pulled straight toward the sphere's center, ending in an unoccupied space as close to the center as possible. A creature that enters the sphere for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, takes 5d10 @force damage, and is restrained until it is no longer in the sphere. If the sphere is in the air, the restrained creature hovers inside the sphere. A creature may use its action to make a STR check. On a success, it is no longer restrained, or may instead free a creature it is able to reach, causing that creature to no longer be restrained.
A creature reduced to 0 hitpoints by this spell is annihilated, along with any nonmagical items it was wearing or carrying.

disintegrate.name: Disintegrate
vsm: a lodestone, and a pinch of dust

desc.desc: A thin, green ray springs from your pointing finger to a target that you can see within range. The target may be a creature, object, or creation of magical force, such as the wall created by a @wall of force spell.

A creature targeted by this spell succeed on a DEX saving throw, or take {*}d6 + 40 @force damage. The target is disintegrated if this damage leaves it with 0 hitpoints. A disintegrated creature, and everything it was wearing and carrying, except magic items, are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. Ths creature may be restored to life only by means of a @true resurrection, or a @wish spell.

This spell automatically disintegrates a Large or smaller nonmagical object, or a creation of magical force. If the target is a Huge or larger object or creation of force, this spell disintegrates a 10ft. cube portion of it. A magic item is unaffected by this spell.

fear.name: Fear
vsm: a white feather, or the heart, of a hen

desc.desc: You project a phantasma image of a creature's worst fears. Each creature in a 30ft. cone must succeed on a WIS saving throw, or drop whatever it is holding and become frightened of you for the duration.

While frightened in this way, a creature must take the @dash action, and move away from you by the safest available route on each of its turns, unless there is nowhere to move. If the creature ends its turn in a location where it doesn't have line of sight of you, the creature may repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

For the duration, you sense the presence of magic within 30ft. of you. Whenever you sense magic in this way, you may use your action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears magic, and you learn its school of magic.
The spell is able to penetrate most barriers, but is blocked by 1ft. of stone, 1in. of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3ft. of wood or dirt.

acid-arrow.name: Acid Arrow
vsm: powdered rhubarb leaf, and an adder's stomach

desc.desc: A shimmering, green arrow streaks toward a target within range, and bursts into a spray of acid. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes {1}d4 @acid damage on a failed save, or half as much on a miss. Additionally, on a hit, the target takes {2}d4 @acid damage at the end of its next turn.

speak-with-dead.name: Speak with Dead
vsm: burning incense

desc.desc: You grant the semblence of life and intelligence to a corpse of your choice within range, allowing it to answer the questions you pose. The corpse must still have a mouth, and cannot be undead. The spell fails if the corpse has already been the target of this spell within the last 10 days.

You may ask the corpse up to 5 questions. The corpse knows only what it knew in life, including the languages it knew. Answers are usually brief, cryptic, or repetitive, and the corpse is under no compulsion to offer a truthful answer if you are hostile to it, or recognizes you as an enemy.

This spell does not return the creature's soul to its body; only its animating spirit. Thus, the corpse cannot learn new information, does not comprehend anything that has happened since it died, and cannot speculate about future events.

vitriolic-sphere.name: Vitriolic Sphere
vsm: a drop of giant slug bile

desc.desc: You point at a space within range, and a glowing, 1ft. ball of emerald acid streaks there, and explodes in a 20ft. radius. Each creature in that area must make a DEX saving throw, taking {*}d4 @acid damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Additionally, on a failure, the target takes 5d4 @acid damage at the end of its next turn.

gaseous-form.name: Gaseous Form
vsm: a bit of gauze, and a wisp of smoke

desc.desc: You transform a willing creature you touch, along with everything it's wearing and carrying, into a misty cloud for the duration. The spell ends if the creature drops to 0 hitpoints. An incorporeal creature is not affected.

While transformed, the target's only method of movement is a flying speed of 10ft. The target may enter and occupy the space of another creature. The target gains resistance to nonmagical damage, and gains advantage on STR, DEX, and CON saving throws. The target may pass through small holes, narrow openings, and even mere cracks, though it treats liquids as though they were solid surfaces. The target cannot fall, and remains hovering in the air, even when stunned, or otherwise incapacitated.

Additionally, the target cannot talk or manipulate objects, and any objects it was carrying or holding cannot be dropped, used, or otherwise interacted with. The target cannot attack, nor cast spells.

aqua-regia.name: Aqua Regia
vsm: the scale of a black dragon

desc.desc: Calling upon alchemical prowess, you create the alchemical acid known as aqua regia; royal water. Royal water is an acid strong enough to dissolve most metals and materials normally used to resist dissolution. This spell can be cast in one of two ways: as an action, or over a longer duration.

If cast as an action, this spell empowers you and any acids originating from your person. For the duration, any spell or effect that deals @acid damage, such as the @acid spray spell, or a thrown acid vial, becomes aqua regia, and deals an additional 4d10 @acid damage.
If cast over 1 minute, you may empower up to 1/2 pint (8 fl oz) of acid into aqua regia permanently. Thrown aqua regia vials deal 4d10 @acid damage.

All @acid damage originating from aqua regia ignores @acid damage resistance, and treats @acid damage immunity as @acid damage resistance. Materials that are normally immune to acid, such as gold and silver, can dissolve in aqua regia.

aqua-regia.source: Azzurey's Destructive Dictionary of Draconic Discord

desc.desc: You hurl a bubble of acid. Choose at most 2 creatures you can see within range, provided they are within 5ft. of each other. A target must succeed on a DEX saving throw, or take {*}d6 @acid damage.
You sap the vitality of a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a CON saving throw, or take {*}d4 @necrotic damage, and fall prone.

Lightning springs from your hand, to deliver a shock to a creature you try to touch. Make a melee spell attack against the target. If the target is wearing armor made of metal, you gain advantage. On a hit, the target takes {*}d8 @lightning damage, and cannot take reactions until the start of its next turn.
You touch a living creature at 0 hitpoints that is not a construct or undead. The creature becomes stable.

thorn-whip.name: Thorn Whip
vsm: the stem of a plant with thorns

desc.desc: You create a long, vine-like whip covered in thorns, that lashes out at your command toward a creature in range. Make a melee spell attack against the target. On a hit, the creature takes {*}d6 @piercing damage, and if the creature is Large or smaller, you may pull the creature up to 10ft. closer to you.

word-of-radiance.name: Word of Radiance
vsm: a holy symbol

desc.desc: You utter a divine word, and burning radiance erupts from you. Any number of creatures of your choice within range must succeed on a CON saving throw, or take {*}d6 @radiant damage.

light.name: Light
vsm: a firefly, or phosphorescent moss

desc.desc: You touch an object that is no larger than 10ft. in any dimension. For the duration, the object sheds bright light in a 20ft. radius, and dim light for another 20ft. The light may be colored as you like. TCompletely covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends early if you cast it again, or dismiss it as an action.
If you target an object held or worn by a hostile creature, that creature must succeed on a DEX saving throw to avoid the spell.

message.name: Message
vsm: a short piece of copper wire

desc.desc: You point your finger toward a creature within range, and whisper a message. The target, and only the target, hears the message, and may reply in a whisper that only you hear.

You may cast this spell through solid objects if you are familiar with the target, and know it is beyond the barrier. The spell is able to penetrate most barriers, but is blocked by magical silence, 1ft. of stone, 1in. of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3ft. of wood or dirt.

A flickering flame appears in your hand. The flame remains there for the duration, and harms neither you nor your equipment. The flame sheds bright light in a 10ft. radius, and dim light for another 10ft. The spell ends if you cast it again, or dismiss it as an action.

You can also attack with the flame, though doing so ends the spell. Whenever you cast this spell, or as an action on a later turn, you may hurl the flame at a creature within 30ft. of you. Make a ranged spell attack. On a hit, the target takes {*}d8 @fire damage.

binding-ice.name: Binding Ice
vsm: a vial of smeltwater

desc.desc: A burst of cold energy emanates from you in a 30ft. cone. Each creature in that area must make a CON saving throw, taking {*}d8 @cold damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Additionally, on a failure, the creature is hindered by ice formations for 1 minute, or until another creature within range uses an action to break away the ice. A hindered creature has its speed reduced to 0.

sleet-storm.name: Sleet Storm
vsm: a pinch of dust, and a few drops of water

desc.desc: For the duration, freezing rain and sleet fall in a 40ft. radius, 20ft. tall cylinder centered on a point you choose within range. The area is heavily obscured, and exposed flames in the area are doused. The ground in the area is covered with slick ice, making it difficult terrain. Whenever a creature enters the spell's area for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a DEX saving throw, or fall prone.
If a creature starts its turn in the spell's area, and is concentrating on a spell, the creature must succeed on a CON saving throw, or lose concentration.

ice-storm.name: Ice Storm
vsm: a pinch of dust, and a few drops of water

desc.desc: A hail of rock-hard ice pounds to the ground in a 20ft. radius, 40ft. high cylinder centered on a point within range. Each creature in the cylinder must make a DEX saving throw, taking {*}d8 @bludgeoning damage + 4d6 @cold damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
Hailstones turn the storm's area into difficult terrain until the end of your next turn.

resistance.name: Resistance
vsm: a miniature cloak

desc.desc: You touch a willing creature. The target may roll 1d4 and add the number rolled to one saving throw of its choice. It may roll the die before, or after the saving throw, its choice. The spell then ends.
You summon fey spirits that take the form of beasts, and appear in unoccupied spaces that you can see within range. Choose one of the following options for what appears:

content.desc: {1} beast(s) of CR 2 or lower.
{2} beasts of CR 1 or lower.
{3} beasts of CR 1/2 or lower.
{4} beasts of CR 1/4 or lower.

desc.desc: Each beast is also considered fey, and it disappears when it drops to 0 hitpoints, or when the spell ends. The summoned creatures are friendly to you and any number of creatures of your choice. Roll initiative for the summoned creatures as a group, which has its own turns. They obey any verbal commands that you issue to them as a free action. If you don't issue any commands to them, they defend themselves from hostile creatures, but otherwise take no actions. The DM has the creature's statistics.

You may blind or deafen foes. Choose {*} creature(s) that you can see within range. A target must succeed on a CON saving throw, or be blinded or deafened, your choice. The target may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

gentle-repose.name: Gentle Repose
vsm: a pinch of salt, and 1cp placed on each of the corpse's eyes, which must remain there for the duration

desc.desc: You touch a corpse, or other remains. For the duration, the target is protected from decay, and cannot become undead.

This spell also effectively extends the time limit on raising the target from the dead, since days spent under the influence of this spell do not count against the time limit of spells such as the @raise dead spell.

animate-dead.name: Animate Dead
vsm: a drop of blood, a piece of flesh, and a pinch of bone dust

desc.desc: This spell creates an undead servant. Choose {1} pile(s) of bones, or {1} corpse(s) of a Medium or Small humanoid within range. Your spell imbues a target with a foul mimicry of life, raising it as an undead creature. The target becomes a skeleton if you chose bones, or a zombie if you chose a corpse. The DM has the creature's game statistics.

As a bonus action on your turn, you may mentally command any creature you made with this spell if the creature is within 60ft. of you. If you control multiple creatures, you may command any, or all of them, at the same time, issuing the same command to each one. You decide what action the creature will take, and where it will move during its next turn, or you may issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor. If you don't issue any commands to it, it defends itself from hostile creatures, but otherwise takes no actions. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is completed.

The creature is under your control for 24 hours, after which it stops obeying any command you've given it. To maintain the control of the creature for another 24 hours, you must cast this spell on the creature again before the current 24 hour period ends. This use of the spell reasserts your control over up to {2} creatures you have animated with this spell, rather than animating a new one.

Necromantic energy washes over a creature of your choice that you can see within range that isn't a construct or undead, draining moisture and vitality from it. The target must make a CON saving throw, taking {*}d8 @necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

If you target a plant creature or magical plant, it gains disadvantage on the saving throw, and the spell deals maximum damage to it. If you target a nonmagical non-creature plant, such as a tree or shrub, the target simply withers and dies, without saving throw.

confusion.name: Confusion
vsm: 3 nut shells

desc.desc: This spell assaults and twists creatures' minds, spawning delusions, and provoking uncontrolled actions. Each creature in a {*}ft. radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range must succeed on a WIS saving throw, or be affected by it. An affected target cannot take reactions, and must roll 1d10 at the start of each of its turns to determine its behavior for that turn.

content: The creature uses all its movement to move in a random direction, determined by rolling 1d8 and assigning a direction to each die face. The creature does not take an action this turn.
The creature does not move or take an action this turn.
The creature uses its action to make a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within its reach. If there is no creature within its reach, the creature does not take an action this turn.
The creature may act and move normally.

desc.desc: A confused creature may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

You create a 20ft. radius sphere of poisonous, yellow fog centered on a point you choose within range. The fog spreads around corners. The fog is dispersed by strong winds, which ends the spell early. The area is heavily obscured.

Whenever a creature enters the spell's area for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, that creature must make a CON saving throw, taking {*}d8 @poison damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Creatures are affected even if they hold their breath, or don't need to breathe.

The fog moves 10ft. away from you at the start of each of your turns, rolling along the surface of the ground. The vapors, being heavier than air, sink to the lowest level of the land, even pouring down openings.
Your touch inflicts disease. Make a melee spell attack against a creature within your reach. On a hit, the target is poisoned.

At the end of each of the poisoned creature's turns, it must make a CON saving throw. On 3 failures, it is no longer poisoned, but is instead afflicted with a disease of your choice, or roll on the table. On 3 successes, it is no longer poisoned, and the spell ends. The successes and failures do not need to be consecutive; keep track of both, until the creature collects 3 of a kind.
Since this spell is a natural disease in its target, any effect that removes a disease, or otherwise ameliorates a disease's effects apply to it.

content: Pain grips the creature's mind, and its eyes turn milky white. The creature gains disadvantage on WIS checks and saving throws, and is blinded.
A raging fever sweeps through the creature's body. The creature gains disadvantage on STR checks, attack rolls, and saving throws.
The creature's flesh decays. The creature gains disadvantage on CHA checks, and vulnerability to all damage.
The creature's mind becomes feverish. The creature gains disadvantage on INT checks and saving throws, and the creature behaves as if under the effects of the @confusion spell during combat.
The creature is overcome with shaking. The creature gains disadvantage on DEX checks, attack rolls, and saving throws.
The creature begins to bleed uncontrollably. The creature gains disadvantage on CON checks and saving throws. Whenever the creature takes damage, it is stunned until the end of its next turn.

spike-growth.name: Spike Growth
vsm: 7 sharp thorns, or 7 small twigs, each sharpened to a point

desc.desc: The ground in a 20ft. radius circle centered on a point within range twists and sprouts hard spikes and thorns. The area becomes difficult terrain. Whenever a creature moves into or within the area, it takes 2d4 @piercing damage for every 5ft. it travels.

The transformation of the ground is camouflaged to look natural. Any creature that cannot see the area at the time the spell is cast must succeed on a Perception (WIS) check to recognize the terrain as hazardous before entering it.
This spell channels vitality into plants within a specific area. There are 2 possible uses for the spell, granting either immediate, or long-term benefits.

If you cast this spell as an action, choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100ft. radius centered on that point become thick and overgrown. A creature moving through the area must spend 4ft. of movement for every 1ft. it moves. You may exclude any number of areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected.

If you cast this spell over 8 hours, you enrich the land. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 1 year, yielding twice the normal amount of food when harvested.

magic-circle.name: Magic Circle
vsm: holy water, or powdered silver and iron worth at least 100gp, which the spell consumes

desc.desc: You create a 10ft. radius, 20ft. tall cylinder of magical energy centered on a point on the ground that you can see within range. Glowing runes appear wherever the cylinder intersects with the floor, or other surface.
Choose any amount of the following types of creatures: celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, or undead. The circle affects a creature of the chosen type in the following ways.

content.desc: The chosen creature type cannot willingly enter the cylinder by nonmagical means. If it tries to use teleportation or interplanar travel to do so, it must first succeed on a CHA saving throw.
The chosen creature type gains disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures within the cylinder.
Creatures within the cylinder cannot by charmed, frightened, or possessed by the chosen creature type.

desc.desc: Whenever you cast this spell, you may choose to cause its magic to operate in the reverse direction, preventing the chosen creature type from leaving the cylinder, and protecting creatures outside it.

freedom-of-movement.name: Freedom of Movement
vsm: a leather strap, bound around the arm, or a similar appendage

desc.desc: You touch a willing creature. For the duration, the target's movement speed is unaffected by difficult terrain, and spells and other effects cannot reduce the target's speed, nor cause the target to be paralyzed or restrained. The target may spend 5ft. of movement to automatically escape from nonmagical restraints, such as manacles, or a grapple. Finally, being underwater imposes no penalty on the target's movements or attacks.

private-sanctum.name: Private Sanctum
vsm: a thin sheet of lead, a piece of opaque glass, a wad of cotton or cloth, and powdered chrysolite

desc.desc: You make an area within range magically secure. The area is a cube that may be as small as 5, to a large as {*}ft. on each side. You may dismiss the spell as an action.
Whenever you cast the spell, choose any amount of the following properties:

content.desc: Sound cannot pass through the barrier at the edge of the warded area.
the barrier of the warded area appears dark and foggy, preventing vision, including darkvision, through it.
Sensors created by divination spells cannot appear inside the protected area, or pass through the barrier at its perimeter.
Creatures in the area cannot be targeted by divination spells.
Nothing may teleport into or out of the warded area.
Planar travel is blocked within the warded area.

desc.desc: Casting this spell on the same spot every day for a year makes this spell permanent.

awaken.name: Awaken
vsm: an agate worth at least 1.000gp, which the spell consumes

desc.desc: After spending the casting time tracing magical pathways within a precious gemstone, you touch a Huge or smaller beast or plant. The target must have either no INT score, or one of 3 or less.

The target gains an INT score of 10, and the ability to speak 1 language you know. If the target is a plant, it gains the ability to move its limbs, roots, vines, creepers, and so forth, and it gains senses similar to a human's. Your DM chooses statistics appopriate for the awakened plant, such as the statistics for the awakened shrub, or awakened tree.

The awakened creature is charmed by you for 30 days, or until you or a creature friendly to you does anything harmful to it. Whenever it stops being charmed, the awakened creature may choose whether to remain friendl to you, based on how you treated it.
You gain the ability to enter a tree, and move from inside it to another tree of the same kind within 500ft.

Both trees must be alive, and at least the same size as you. You must use 5ft. of movement to enter a tree. You instantly know the location of all other trees of the same kind within 500ft. of you, and, as part of the move used to enter the tree, may either pass into one of those trees, or step out of the tree you're in. You appear in a spot of your choice within 5ft. of the destination tree, using another 5ft. of movement. If you have no movement left, you appear within 5ft. of the tree you entered.
You may use this transportation ability once per round. You must end each turn outside a tree.
You touch a creature. The creature must succeed on a WIS saving throw, or become cursed. Whenever you cast this spell, choose one of the following:

content.desc: Choose an ability score. While cursed, the target gains disability on ability checks and saving throws made with that ability score.
While cursed, the target gains disadvantage on attack rolls against you.
While cursed, at the start of each of its turns, the target must succeed on a WIS saving throw or waste its action doing nothing that turn.
While cursed, your attacks and spells deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage to the target.

desc.desc: A @remove curse spell ends this effect. At the DM's discretion, you may choose an alternative curse effect, but it should be no more powerful than those described above. The DM has final say on such a curse's effect.

tiny-hut.name: Tiny Hut
vsm: a small, crystal bead

desc.desc: A 10ft. radius, immobile dome of force springs into existence around and above you, and remains stationary for the duration. The spell ends early if you leave its area.

The dome fits up to 9 creatures of Medium size or smaller. If the area includes a larger creature, or more than 9 creatures, the spell fails. Creatures and objects within the dome when you cast the spell may move through it freely. All other creatures and objects are barred from passing through it. Spells and other magical effects cannot extend through the dome, or be cast through it. The atmosphere inside the dome is comfortable and dry, regardless of the weather outside.
You may command the interior to become dimly lit, or dark. The dome is opaque from the outside, any color you choose, and is transparent from the inside.

You touch a creature, and grant it a measure of protection from death. The first time the target would drop to 0 hitpoints as a result of taking damage, the target instead drops to 1 hitpoints, and the spell ends.
Alternatively, if the target is subjected to an effect that would kill it instantly without dealing damage, the effect is negated against the target, and the spell ends.

hold-monster.name: Hold Monster
vsm: a small, straight piece of iron

desc.desc: Choose a creature that is not undead you can see within range. The creature must succeed on a WIS saving throw, or be paralyzed. The creature may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

dream.name: Dream
vsm: a handful of sand, a dab of ink, and a writing quill plucked from a sleeping bird

desc.desc: This spell shapes a creature's dreams. Choose a creature known to you as the target of this spell. The target must be on the same plane of existence as you. Creature that do not sleep, such as elves, cannot be contacted by this spell. You, or a willing creature you touch, enters a trance state, acting as a messenger. While in the trance, the messenger is aware of their surroundings, but cannot take actions, or move.

If the target is asleep, the messenger appears in the target's dreams, and may converse with the target as long as it remains asleep. The messenger may also shape the environment of the dream, creating landscapes, objects, and other images. The messenger may emerge from the trance at any time, ending the effect of the spell early. The target recalls the dream perfectly upon waking. If the target is awake when you cast the spell, the messenger knows it, and may either end the trance and the spell, or wait for the target to fall asleep, at which point the messenger appears in the target's dreams.

You may make the messenger appear monstrous and terrifying to the target. If you do, the messenger may deliver a message of no more than 10 words, and then the target must make a WIS saving throw. On a failure, echoes of the phantasmal monstrosity spawn a nightmare that lasts the duration of the target's sleep, and prevents the target from gaining any benefit from that rest. Additionally, the target takes 3d6 @psychic damage once awoken.
If you have a body part, lock of hair, clipping from a nail, or similar portion of the target's body, the target gains disadvantage on the saving throw.

scrying.name: Scrying
vsm: a focus worth at least 1.000gp, such as a crystal ball, silver mirror, or a font willed with holy water

desc.desc: You may see and hear a particular creature you choose that is on the same plane of existence as you. The target must make a WIS saving throw. On a failure, the spell creates an invisible sensor within 10ft. of the target. You are able to see and hear through the sensor as if you were there. The sensor moves with the target, remaining within 10ft. of it for the duration. On a success, the target is unaffected, and cannot you cannot target it with another casting of this spell for 24 hours. A creature that is able to see invisible objects sees the sensor as a luminous orb, about the size of your fist.
The saving throw DC is modified based on your connection and knowledge to the target, as follows:

content: You have heard of the target.
Body part, lock of hair, bit of nail, or the like

desc.desc: Instead of targeting a creature, you may choose a location you have seen before as the target of this spell. If you do, the sensor appears at that location, and does not move.

teleportation-circle.name: Teleportation Circle
vsm: rare chalks and inks infused with precious gems worth 50gp, which the spell consumes

desc.desc: You draw a 10ft. diameter dircle on the ground, inscribed with sigils that link your location to a permanent teleportation circle of your choice whose sigil sequence you know, and that is on the same plane of existence as you. A shimmering portal opens within the circle you drew, and remains open until the end of your next turn. Any creature that enters the portal instantly appears within 5ft. of the destination circle, or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

Many major temples, guilds, and other important places have permanent teleportation circles inscribed somewhere within their confines. Each such circle includes a unique sigil sequence - a string of magical runes arranged in a particular pattern. When you first gain the ability to cast this spell, you learn the sigil sequences of 2 destinations on the Material Plane, determined by the DM. You may learn additional sigil sequences during your adventures, which requires studying a new one for 1 minute.
You may create a permanent teleportation circle by casting this spell in the same location every day for 1 year. You need not use the circle to teleport when you cast the spell in this way.

slow.name: Slow
vsm: a drop of molasses

desc.desc: You alter time around up to 6 creatures of your choice within range, provided they fit into a 40ft. cube. Each target must succeed on a WIS saving throw, or be affected by this spell. An affected target's speed is halved, suffers -2 AC, -2 to DEX saving throws, and cannot use reactions. On its turn, it may use either an action, or a bonus action, but not both. Regardless of the creature's abilities or magic items, it cannot make more than 1 melee or ranged attack during its turn.

If the creature attempts to cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action, roll 1d20. On an 11 or higher, the spell doesn't take effect until the creature's next turn, and the creature must use its action on that turn to complete the spell. If it can't, the spell fails.
An affected creature may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

You briefly become one with nature, and gain knowledge of the surrounding territory. In the outdoors, the spell gives you knowledge of the land within 3mi. of you. In caves and other natural underground settings, the radius is limited to 300ft. The spell does not function where nature has been replaced by construction, such as in dungeons and towns.
You instantly gain knowledge of up to 3 facts of your choice about any of the following subjects as they relate to the area:

content.desc: Terrain, and bodies of water.
Prevalent plants, minerals, animals, or peoples.
Powerful celestials, fey, fiends, elementals, or undead.
Influence from other planes of existence.
Buildings.

desc.desc: For example, you could determine the location of powerful undead in the area, the location of major sources of safe drinking water, and the location of any nearby towns.

cone-of-cold.name: Cone of Cold
vsm: a small crystal or glass cone

desc.desc: A blast of cold air erupts from your hands. Each creature in a 60ft. cone must make a CON saving throw, taking {*}d8 @cold damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. A creature killed by this spell becomes a frozen statue until thawed.
Briefly surrounded by silvery mist, you teleport up to 30ft. to an unoccupied space you can see.

water-breathing.name: Water Breathing
vsm: a short reed, or piece of straw

desc.desc: This spell grants up to 10 willing creature you can see within range the ability to breathe underwater until the spell ends. Affected creatures retain their normal mode of respiration.

water-walk.name: Water Walk
vsm: a piece of cork

desc.desc: This spell grants up to 10 willing creature you can see within range the ability to move across any liquid surface, such as water, acid, mud, snow, quicksand, or lava, as if it were harmless solid ground. Creatures crossing molten lava may still take damage from the heat. If you target a creature submerged in a liquid, the spell carries the target to the surface of the liquid at a rate of 60ft. per round.

control-water.name: Control Water
vsm: a drop of water, and a pinch of dust

desc.desc: You control any freestanding water inside an area you choose that fits in a cube no more than 100ft. on one side. You may choose from any of the following effects when you cast this spell. As an action, you may repeat the same effect, or choose a different one.

content.name: Flood
content.desc: You cause the water level of all standing water in the area to rise by as much as 20ft. If the area includes a shore, the flooding water spills over onto dry land. If you choose an area in a large body of water, you instead create a 20ft. tall wave that travels from one side of the area to the other, and then crashes down. Any Huge or smaller vehicles in the wave's path are carried with it to the other side. Any Huge or smaller vehicles struck by the wave must roll 1d4. On a 1, it capsizes. The water level remains elevated until the spell ends, or you choose a different effect. If the effect produced a wave, the wave repeats on the start of your next turn while the flood effect lasts.

content.name: Part Water
content.desc: You cause water in the area to move apart, and create a trench. The trench extends across the spell's area, and the separated water forms a wall to either side. The trench remains until the spell ends, or you choose a different effect. The water then slowly fills in the trench over the course of the next round, until the normal water level is restored.

content.name: Redirect Flow
content.desc: You cause flowing water in the are to move in a direction you choose, even if the water has to flow over obstacles, up walls, or in other unlikely directions. The water in the area moves as you direct it, but once it moves beyond the spell's area, it resumes its flow based on the terrain. The water continues to move in the direction you chose until the spell ends, or you choose a different effect.

content.name: Whirlpool
content.desc: This effect requires a body of water at least 50ft. across, and 25ft. deep. You cause a whirlpool to form in the center of the area. The whirlpool forms a vortex that is 5ft. wide at the base, up to 50ft. wide at the top, and 25ft. tall. Any creature or object in the water, and within 25ft. of the vortex is pulled 10ft. toward it. A creature may swim away from the vortex by making an Athletics (STR) check. Whenever a creature enters the vortext for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, it must make a STR saving throw, taking 2d8 @bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Additionally, on a failure, the creature is caught in the vortext. A caught creature may use its action to try and swim away from the vortex as described above, but gains disadvantage on the Athletics (STR) check to do so. Objects take 2d8 @bludgeoning damage the first time it enters the vortex, and every round it remains there thereafter.

conjure-elemental.name: Conjure Elemental
vsm: burning incense for air, soft clay for earth, sulfur and phosphorus for fire, or water and sand for water

desc.desc: You call forth an elemental servant. Choose an area of air, earth, fire, or water that fills a 10ft. cube within range. An elemental of CR {*} or lower, appropriate to the area you chose, appears in an unoccupied space within 10ft. of it. For example, a fire elemental may emerge from a bonfire, or an earth elemental rises up from the ground. The elemental disappears when it drops to 0 hitpoints, or when the spell ends.

The elemental is friendly to you and any number of creatures of your choice for the duration. Roll initiative for the elemental, which has its own turns. It obeys any verbal commands that you issue to it as a free action. If you don't issue any commands to the elemental, it defends itself from hostile creatures, but otherwise takes no actions.

If your concentration is broken, the elemental doesn't disappear. Instead, you lose control of the elemental, it may become hostile to you, and it might attack. An uncontrolled elemental cannot be dismissed, and it disappears 1 hour after you summon it. The DM has the elemental's statistics.

You create 45lbs. of food, and 30gal. of water on the ground, or in containers within range, enough to sustain up to 15 humanoids, or 5 steeds for 24 hours. The food is bland but nourishing, and spoils if uneaten for 24 hours. The water is clean, and doesn't spoil.
You touch a willing creature, and grant it one damage type of your choice: @acid, @cold, @fire, @lightning, or @thunder.

hallucinatory-terrain.name: Hallucinatory Terrain
vsm: a stone, a twig, and a bit of green plant

desc.desc: You make natural terrain that fits in a 150ft. cube look, sound, and smell like some other sort of natural terrain. Thus, open fields or a road may be made to resemble a swamp, hill, crevasse, or some other difficult or impassable terrain. A pond may be made to seem like a grassy meadow, a precipice like a gentle slope, or a rock-strewn gully like a wide and smooth road. Manufactured structures, equipment, and creatures within the area aren't changed in appearance.

The tactile characteristics of the terrain are unchanged, so creatures entering the area are likely to see through the illusion. If the difference isn't obvious by touch, a creature carefully examining the illusion may attempt an Investigation (INT) to disbelieve it. A creature who discerns the illusion for what it is, sees it as a vague image superimposed on the terrain.

insect-plague.name: Insect Plague
vsm: a few grains of sugar, some kernals of grain, and a smear of fat

desc.desc: Swarming, biting locusts fill a 20ft. radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range. The sphere spreads around corners. The sphere is lightly obscured, and difficult terrain.

When the area appears, and when a creature enters the spell's area for the first time on its turn, or ends its turn there, it must make a CON saving throw, taking {*}d10 @piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

wall-of-stone.name: Wall of Stone
vsm: a small block of granite

desc.desc: A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into existence at a point you choose within range. The wall is 6in. thick, and is composed of 10 10ft. by 10ft. panels. Each panel must be contiguous with at least one other panel. Alternatively, you may create 10ft. by 20ft. panels that are only 3in. thick.

If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pused to one side of the wall of your choice. If a creature would be surrounded on all sides by the wall, or the wall and another surface, that creature may make a DEX saving throw. On a success, as a reaction, it may move up to its speed so that it is no longer enclosed by the wall.

The wall may have any shape you desire, though it cannot occupy the same space as a creature or object. The wall doesn't need to be vertical, or resting on any firm foundation. It must, however, merge with, and be solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you may use this spell to bridge a chasm, or create a ram. If you create a span greater than 20ft. in length, you must halve the size of each panel to create supports. You may crudely shape the wall to create crenellations, battlements, and so on.

The wall is an object made of stone that can be damaged, and thus breached. Each panel has 15 AC, and 30 hitpoints per in. of thickness. Reducing a panel to 0 hitpoints destroys it, and may cause connected panels to collapse at the DM's discretion.
If you maintain your concentration on this spell for its whole duration, the wall becomes permanent, and cannot be dispelled.
